newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slide lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slide lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slid sharply at the start of trade on Thursday morning in line with bearish sentiment seen on Wall Street overnight, and brokers were cautious on the medium-term outlook.
"We still need to wait until the Dow shows a clear direction," said Francis Wu, institutional sales manager at Mansion House Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was trading 78 points lower at 12,058 in early trade, after hitting an opening low of 12,013.51. Turnover was a respectable HK$754 million.
The Dow Industrials lost 94.04 points, or 1.42 percent, overnight to close at 6,517.01.
Analysts said the U.S. market was worried the U.S. Federal Reserve may raise rates further following last week's increase of short-term interest rates.

Several Hong Kong-based brokers are taking the view that the Federal Reserve's March 25 interest rate hike was a pre-emptive anti-inflationary strike and not the start of a long-term gradual uptrend in rates, analysts said.
"It's too late to be bearish," said one broker with a large regional house, adding the market's valuation had fallen to an attractive level.
The April Hang Seng Index Futures contract was trading 62 points down at 11,973, off it low of 11,890.
The property sector was relatively stable after the sell off on Tuesday, while the banks came under renewed selling pressure.
H shares bucked the market's negative trend to show the only sector gain in early trade.
Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings slipped HK$1.00 to HK$176.50. Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank was unchanged at HK$77.75.

In the H share sector, Qingling Motors Ltd was chiefly responsible for lifting the sector. The share added HK$0.125 to HK$4.10, but on thin trade of only HK$3.13 million. Shenzhen Expressway added HK$0.05 to HK$2.45.
Red chip newcomer Guangnan (Holdings), which will report its 1996 annual results later on Thursday, slipped HK$0.10 to HK$9.85.
Sports shoe manufacturer Yue Yuen Industries was the best performer, gaining HK$1.00 to HK$18.70 in early trade.
